_llm_instructions:
Fill out the 'project_title', 'date_prepared' properties, and the 'value' properties for each field in this REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENTATION template based on the provided project context. Context & Definition: The requirements documentation assists the project manager in making tradeoff decisions among requirements and in managing stakeholder expectations. Requirements will be progressively elaborated as more information about the project becomes available. Requirements documentation is an output from the process 5.2 Collect Requirements in the PMBOK® Guide – Sixth Edition. Alignment: The requirements documentation should be aligned and consistent with the following documents:
• Requirements management plan
• Benefits management plan
• Quality management plan
• Requirements traceability matrix
• Release plan

Requirements List.guidance:
Generate a JSON array of objects representing the Requirements table. Each object must have the exact keys specified below. Generate at least 5 representative requirements based on the project context, ensuring they cover various categories (Business, Stakeholder, Solution, Quality).
Rules:
- 'ID': Create a unique identifier for the requirement (e.g., REQ-001).
- 'Requirement': Clearly articulate the specific condition or capability.
- 'Stakeholder': Name, role, or organization of the stakeholder.
- 'Category': Classify the requirement (e.g., Business, Stakeholder, Solution, Quality).
- 'Priority': Assign a priority level (e.g., High, Medium, Low).
- 'Acceptance criteria': Specific, measurable criteria that must be met.
- 'Test or verification method': Method to verify fulfillment (e.g., Inspection, Test).
- 'Phase or release': Project phase, sprint, or product release.
- 'Dependencies': IDs of any other requirements that this requirement depends on.
- 'Assumptions & Constraints': Any assumptions made or technical/business constraints.
